definitions.gloss: to throw out; to toss out
definitions.explanation: To physically throw or toss something out carelessly.

definitions.gloss: to abandon; to give up on; to quit halfway
definitions.explanation: To abandon a task, responsibility, or commitment partway through. Often implies irresponsibility or frustration.

examples.japanese: ゴミを{外|そと}に{放|ほう}り{出|だ}した。
{荷物|にもつ}を{玄関|げんかん}に{放|ほう}り{出|だ}して{走|はし}って{行|い}った。
examples.english: He tossed his bags at the entrance and ran off.

examples.japanese: {重|おも}すぎて、{思|おも}わず{荷物|にもつ}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}してしまった。
examples.english: It was so heavy that I involuntarily tossed the luggage down.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}すわけにはいかない。
examples.english: I can't just abandon my work.

examples.japanese: {途中|とちゅう}で{勉強|べんきょう}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I gave up studying halfway through.

examples.japanese: {責任|せきにん}ある{立場|たちば}にいるのに、すべてを{放|ほう}り{出|だ}して{辞|や}めてしまった。
examples.english: Despite being in a position of responsibility, he abandoned everything and quit.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Godan verb (す ending, conjugates as s-row: {放|ほう}り{出|だ}さない, {放|ほう}り{出|だ}します). Transitive — takes a direct object marked with を.

USAGE:
Sense 1 (physical throwing) often implies carelessness. Sense 2 (abandoning) is more common in daily conversation and implies giving up irresponsibly. The figurative sense frequently collocates with {仕事|しごと} (work) or {勉強|べんきょう} (study).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {仕事|しごと}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}す (to abandon one's work)
- {勉強|べんきょう}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}す (to give up studying)
- {途中|とちゅう}で{放|ほう}り{出|だ}す (to quit midway)
- {荷物|にもつ}を{放|ほう}り{出|だ}す (to toss luggage aside)
